| [`mainframe.cpu`](/docs/registry/mainframe/entities.md#mainframecpu) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | A physical mainframe processor within the Central Processing Complex (CPC) — the mainframe equivalent of a CPU core in a distributed server. |
| [`mainframe.partition.nic`](/docs/registry/mainframe/entities.md#mainframepartitionnic) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | A virtual network interface card (NIC) attached to a logical partition (LPAR) in Dynamic Partition Manager (DPM) mode — the mainframe equivalent of a vNIC attached to a virtual machine. |

Analogous to a Kubernetes Persistent Volume or a cloud block storage volume. |

| [`refinement.mainframe.host`](/docs/registry/mainframe/entity-refinements.md#refinementmainframehost) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | Mainframe refinement of the generic host entity for the IBM Z Central Processing Complex (CPC). A CPC is a physical bare-metal server — the mainframe equivalent of any host. The IBM Z-specific attributes (serial number, machine type, machine model) extend the generic host description while preserving full compatibility with consumers that understand the base host entity. |
| [`refinement.mainframe.host.virtualization.platform`](/docs/registry/mainframe/entity-refinements.md#refinementmainframehostvirtualizationplatform) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | Mainframe refinement of virtualization.platform for the IBM Z Central Processing Complex (CPC). A CPC is a physical computing platform that hosts firmware-enforced logical partitions (LPARs) via PR/SM, directly analogous to virtualization.platform in the generic virtualization schema. |
| [`refinement.mainframe.partition.virtualization.partition`](/docs/registry/mainframe/entity-refinements.md#refinementmainframepartitionvirtualizationpartition) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | Mainframe refinement of virtualization.partition for an IBM Z logical partition (LPAR).  An LPAR is a firmware-enforced partition managed by PR/SM, directly analogous to virtualization.partition in the generic virtualization schema. |
| [`refinement.mainframe.processor_pool.virtualization.resource_pool`](/docs/registry/mainframe/entity-refinements.md#refinementmainframeprocessor_poolvirtualizationresource_pool) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | Mainframe refinement of virtualization.resource_pool for an IBM Z shared processor pool. A shared processor pool defines a capacity boundary for a group of physical processor engines (CP, IFL, zIIP, ICF) shared by logical partitions, directly analogous to virtualization.resource_pool in the generic virtualization schema. |
| [`refinement.mainframe.storage_group.virtualization.storage_pool`](/docs/registry/mainframe/entity-refinements.md#refinementmainframestorage_groupvirtualizationstorage_pool) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | Mainframe refinement of virtualization.storage_pool for an IBM Z DPM storage group. A storage group aggregates FCP/SCSI or FICON/ECKD volumes allocated to partitions and guests, directly analogous to virtualization.storage_pool in the generic virtualization schema. |
| [`refinement.mainframe.vswitch.virtualization.vswitch`](/docs/registry/mainframe/entity-refinements.md#refinementmainframevswitchvirtualizationvswitch) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | Mainframe refinement of virtualization.vswitch for an IBM z/VM VSWITCH or DPM virtual switch. A mainframe virtual switch bridges partitions and guest VMs to physical OSA-Express or RoCE network adapters, directly analogous to virtualization.vswitch in the generic virtualization schema. |
| [`refinement.mainframe.zvm.guest.virtualization.vm`](/docs/registry/mainframe/entity-refinements.md#refinementmainframezvmguestvirtualizationvm) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | Mainframe refinement of virtualization.vm for an IBM z/VM guest virtual machine. A z/VM guest is a virtual machine managed by the z/VM Control Program (CP), running Linux on Z or z/OS, directly analogous to virtualization.vm in the generic virtualization schema. |
| [`refinement.mainframe.zvm.hypervisor.virtualization.hypervisor`](/docs/registry/mainframe/entity-refinements.md#refinementmainframezvmhypervisorvirtualizationhypervisor) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | Mainframe refinement of virtualization.hypervisor for the z/VM Control Program (CP). z/VM is a Type-1 software hypervisor that runs on IBM Z hardware (bare-metal or inside a PR/SM LPAR) and manages hundreds to thousands of guest virtual machines, directly analogous to virtualization.hypervisor in the generic virtualization schema. |

**[1] `mainframe.adapter.name`:** The channel subsystem (CSS) index and channel path identifier (CHPID) are concatenated with a dot separator, e.g., "0.2D" for CSS 0, CHPID 2D. Reported by the HMC Web Services API adapter object field `adapter-id`.

**[2] `mainframe.adapter.owning.partition`:** Derived from the IBM Z HMC Web Services API adapter object property `partitions-assigned-to-adapter`, an array of assigned-partition-info objects. Set to 'shared' when more than one partition is assigned.

**[3] `mainframe.adapter.port.id`:** Reported by the HMC Web Services API network-physical-adapter-port metric group field `network-port-id`. In distributed systems terms, this is analogous to the port number on a multi-port NIC.

**[4] `mainframe.adapter.status`:** Reported by the HMC Web Services API adapter object field `status` (DPM mode).

**[5] `mainframe.adapter.type`:** Reported by the HMC Web Services API adapter object field `type`. Used to distinguish network, storage, cryptographic, and accelerator adapters when aggregating per-type utilization metrics.

**[6] `mainframe.channel.id`:** Reported by the HMC Web Services API channel-path object. In distributed systems terms, this is analogous to a storage HBA port or channel identifier.

**[7] `mainframe.channel.name`:** The channel subsystem (CSS) index and channel path identifier (CHPID) are concatenated with a dot separator, e.g., "0.2D" for CSS 0, CHPID 2D. Reported by the HMC Web Services API channel-path object.

**[8] `mainframe.channel.owning.partition`:** Reported by the IBM Z HMC Web Services API `channel-usage` metric group field `logical-partition-name`. The field is 'shared' when the channel is shared across partitions, and an empty string for channel types that do not expose an owning partition (for example coupling channels).

**[9] `mainframe.channel.type`:** Reported by the IBM Z HMC Web Services API adapter object property `type`, whose values include `ficon`, `osa`, `hipersockets` and `network-express`.

**[10] `mainframe.cpu.name`:** Reported by the HMC Web Services API processor object. In distributed systems terms, a mainframe processor is analogous to a physical CPU core.

**[11] `mainframe.host.machine_model`:** Reported by the HMC Web Services API CPC object field `machine-model`. Combined with `mainframe.host.machine_type`, forms the full IBM machine type-model identifier (e.g., "9175-ME1").

**[12] `mainframe.host.machine_type`:** Reported by the HMC Web Services API CPC object field `machine-type`. In distributed systems terms, this is analogous to the CPU family or server product line identifier.

**[13] `mainframe.host.serial_number`:** Reported by the HMC Web Services API CPC object field `serial-number`. The serial number uniquely identifies a physical mainframe machine.

**[14] `mainframe.partition.memory.type`:** Reported by the HMC Web Services API partition object storage allocation properties. Central storage is equivalent to RAM; expanded storage is an additional address extension beyond central storage. IBM Virtual Flash Memory (VFM) is a solid-state tier extending the memory address space.

**[15] `mainframe.partition.name`:** A logical partition (LPAR) is the mainframe equivalent of a virtual machine (VM) in distributed cloud environments. Each LPAR can run an independent operating system such as z/OS, Linux, or z/VM. Reported by the HMC Web Services API partition object field `name`.

**[16] `mainframe.partition.nic.name`:** Reported by the HMC Web Services API partition-attached-network-interface metric group. In distributed systems terms, this is analogous to a virtual NIC (vNIC) attached to a virtual machine.

**[17] `mainframe.partition.number`:** Each logical partition on an IBM Z Central Processing Complex (CPC) is assigned a unique partition number (1–64) by the Processor Resource/Systems Manager (PR/SM). The partition number is static for the lifetime of the LPAR configuration. In distributed systems terms, this is analogous to a slot index or NUMA node number — a small integer that identifies a hardware-allocated execution domain. Reported by the HMC Web Services API logical-partition object field `partition-number` (Classic mode). Not applicable in DPM mode where partitions are identified by UUID only.

**[18] `mainframe.partition.status`:** In classic mode (LPAR), reported by the HMC Web Services API partition object field `status` with values: operating, not-operating, not-activated, exceptions. In DPM mode, reported with values: active, degraded, paused, stopped, starting, stopping, reservation-error, terminated, communications-not-active, status-check.

**[19] `mainframe.partition.type`:** IBM Z Processor Resource/Systems Manager (PR/SM) and Dynamic Partition Manager (DPM) classify each partition by its intended workload type. This controls which processor types the partition may use and which IBM Z software licences apply. In distributed systems terms, this is analogous to an instance type or VM profile that constrains what workloads can run on it. Reported by the HMC Web Services API logical-partition or partition object field `partition-type`.

**[20] `mainframe.smc.type`:** Shared Memory Communications (SMC) has two variants: SMC-D uses the Internal Shared Memory (ISM) virtual PCI device for intra-CPC communication, while SMC-R uses RDMA over Converged Ethernet (RoCE) for inter-CPC or CPC-to-external communication. No IBM Z HMC Web Services API source is currently known for this attribute — SC27-2646-01 declares no SMC telemetry metric group. Populate it from an in-band source. In distributed systems terms, these are analogous to shared-memory IPC and RDMA transports respectively.

**[21] `mainframe.storage.fulfillment.state`:** Reported by the HMC Web Services API storage-group or storage-volume object field `fulfillment-state` (DPM mode only, HMC ≥ 2.14.1). In distributed systems terms, this is analogous to the binding phase of a Kubernetes Persistent Volume Claim.

**[22] `mainframe.storage.group.name`:** Reported by the HMC Web Services API storage-group resource object field `name` (DPM mode only, HMC ≥ 2.14.1). A storage group aggregates storage volumes of the same connectivity type (FCP, FC, NVMe) that are managed together and can be attached to partitions.

**[23] `mainframe.storage.group.type`:** Reported by the HMC Web Services API storage-group object field `type` (DPM mode only, HMC ≥ 2.14.1).

**[24] `mainframe.storage.group.volume.name`:** Reported by the HMC Web Services API storage-volume resource object field `name` (DPM mode only, HMC ≥ 2.14.1). A storage volume is a single logical unit of block storage (LUN / ECKD DASD cylinder set / NVMe namespace) within a storage group.

**[25] `mainframe.vswitch.name`:** On IBM z/VM, a virtual switch (VSWITCH) is a software-defined Ethernet switch managed by the z/VM Control Program (CP). It connects z/VM guest virtual machines to each other and to physical network adapters (OSA-Express, RoCE). The VSWITCH name is 1–8 uppercase alphanumeric characters defined in the z/VM CP directory. In IBM Z Dynamic Partition Manager (DPM) mode, virtual switches are exposed as `virtual-switch` objects in the HMC Web Services API. In distributed systems terms, a mainframe virtual switch is analogous to an OVS bridge or a VMware vSwitch. Reported by the HMC Web Services API as the `name` field of the virtual-switch object.

**[26] `mainframe.zvm.guest.userid`:** Each z/VM guest is identified by a unique userid defined in the z/VM CP user directory. The userid is the z/VM equivalent of a virtual machine name on other hypervisor platforms (e.g., a VMware VM name or a KVM domain name). Userids are 1–8 uppercase alphanumeric characters. In distributed systems terms, this is analogous to a virtual machine name or container name. Reported by the HMC Web Services API as the `zvm-guest-name` field on the logical-partition object when the partition is running as a z/VM guest.

**[27] `mainframe.zvm.hypervisor.name`:** The z/VM (z/Virtual Machine) Control Program (CP) runs as a software hypervisor inside a PR/SM logical partition (LPAR). The hypervisor instance is identified by the LPAR name that hosts it. In distributed systems terms, this is analogous to the hypervisor hostname. Reported by the HMC Web Services API as the `name` field of the logical-partition object that contains the z/VM instance.

| `maximum` | The maximum processor weight the partition may consume when spare capacity is available. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `minimum` | The minimum processor weight guaranteed to the partition, below which its allocation will not fall. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
